title: {Syn} The Birthday Paradox Is a Crowd Illusion
content:
In a group of 23 people, the chance that at least two share a birthday is a little over 50 percent, ignoring leap days and uneven birth rates.

The surprise comes from counting pairs. Twenty-three people create 253 possible pairs, so coincidences arrive faster than intuition expects.

Why it matters: probability keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
